newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares close down, blue chips seen soft.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares close down, blue chips seen soft.

text.p: Property stocks led the Singapore market lower at the close on Tuesday. Dealers said they expected prices of blue chips including property stocks to ease further in the short term.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index slipped 5.47 points to 2,171.69. Market volume was mild at 89.25 million shares with declines ahead of rises by 175 to 136.

"Property stocks seem to be taking the brunt of the losses," said an institutional dealer. He said investors were spooked by reports of softening rentals in both the residential and commercial sectors.
Dealers said broking houses were also lowering their full-year earnings forecast of Singapore companies after a lacklustre first-half reporting season which just ended.
"The market is going to come off some more and should stabilise around the 2,100 level. I would buy blue chips when it gets to that level and sell on the way up," said a dealer.

City Development headed losses in the property sector, down by Singapore S$0.50 to S$11.50 on 856,000 shares. Singapore Telecom fell S$0.04 to S$3.20 on heavy volume of 4.5 million shares and Keppel Corp lost S$0.40 to S$10.50 on 1.2 million shares.-- JOSEPHINE NG (65-8703094)
